Date: 2026-11-08T15:14:22Z
Subject: FiskPay API 504 spike — regions us-west/us-east intermittently 504

Team,

We started seeing a spike in 504s from our payment submission path around 15:05 UTC. Impacting roughly 12% of production transactions for ~20m intervals, then falling back, then spiking again. Attached traceroutes and a sampling of request ids.

Symptoms:
- 504s from Redwood endpoint: /v1/generate -> upstream timeout
- Error surge aligns with small bursts of increased latency from 70ms -> 700ms on some probes
- Traceroutes show asymmetric hops when the problem occurs (one path goes through a proxy cluster that later times out)

We are in a live campaign and this is hitting production. Can you confirm receipt and next steps? We can make a packet capture window if needed.

Thanks,
Alan
Lead SRE, FiskPay

Subject: Re: FiskPay API 504 spike — initial triage notes

Quick triage notes (15:30-15:38 UTC):
- Correlation: 504 spike aligns with transient BGP withdraws from a subset of host routes in our us-west peering cluster. We see route flaps originating from a transit provider handoff that routes through a proxy tier.
- Proxy pool: 3 of 18 proxies started returning 504s and TCP retransmits increased for connections that traversed those proxies.
- DNS: FiskPay TTLs are 60s. When the path fails, clients hit fallback which can take 60s+ depending on caches. However, traceroutes show asymmetric hops on failing requests (sometimes diverted through an on-path firewall that is overloaded).
- Hypothesis: A transient upstream peering flap combined with our proxy health checks not failing fast enough is causing slow failover and extended 504 windows. Firewall ACL reuse on the path may be amplifying timeouts.

Immediate actions taken (15:34 UTC):
- Removed the 3 degraded proxies from the pool (manual drain), started routing traffic away.
- Instructed infra to increase proxy health-check frequency to 5s for FiskPay routes.
- Opened ticket with the transit provider; waiting confirmation on reported withdraws.

Attachments: sample-logs-excerpt (included in Alan’s zip)

Next steps: coordinate temporary bypass of the on-path proxy cluster for critical FiskPay transactions and evaluate whether a dedicated egress path (different peering/transit) is necessary.

- Rafael
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec: FiskPay SEV1 — state, impact, proposed mitigations

Vivek / Marissa —

Summary: FiskPay (large merchant, active campaign) is seeing intermittent 504/timeouts affecting ~10–15% of payment submissions during spikes. We have confirmed transient route withdraws and a cluster of proxies returning 504s. Initial mitigation reduced error rate from ~15% -> ~4% after draining three proxies and increasing health-check frequency.

Impact: production revenue risk; customer is requesting credits and an RCA; if we see reoccurrence, they will escalate to legal/comms.

Proposed mitigations (recommendations):
- Short term (now): move FiskPay traffic to alternate egress pool + keep degraded proxies drained; extend sticky session TTL to reduce churn during probe windows.
- Mid term (24–72h): provision a dedicated egress path for FiskPay (reserved capacity) while we evaluate transit vendor instability; increase probe sensitivity and lower DNS TTL caching for critical endpoints.
- Communication: offer FiskPay a usage credit for the incident window and daily sync until RCA complete.

Requesting authorization to:
1) Approve expedited reservation of a small dedicated egress capacity for FiskPay (cost estimate attached in infra request),
2) Authorize a 10% credit for impacted volume during the incident window (we can finalize after RCA),
3) Join a customer-facing call (I can run ops updates).

I’ll keep this thread for internal exec updates and use the JIRA ticket INF-4721 for the RCA artifacts.

— Olga

FiskPay asks for:
- RCA within 48h including the transit provider’s confirmation of withdraws and why proxy health checks did not fail faster
- Formal credit proposal (if you authorize 10% we will accept that as a starting point)
- Timeline for the dedicated egress option and any changes to DNS TTL behavior that may reduce failover time

We’ll keep our packet captures available if you need deeper traces.

Appreciate the quick remediation.

— Alan
